title: Science and measurement
summary: Forces, quantities and the words for measuring them.

questions.clue: This is the force that pulls every object towards the centre of the earth.
questions.note: Gravity is the force; weight is what it produces on a given mass. Mass itself does not change with location.

questions.clue: This is what a liquid does when it turns into a gas, such as a puddle drying in the sun.
questions.note: The reverse, a gas becoming a liquid, is condensation. Boiling is evaporation throughout the liquid rather than at its surface.

questions.clue: This is the resistance felt when one surface rubs against another.
questions.note: It converts movement into heat, which is why rubbing your hands together warms them.

questions.clue: This is the distance straight across a circle, passing through its centre.
questions.note: Half of it is the radius, and the distance all the way round the outside is the circumference.

questions.clue: This is the distance all the way around the outside of a circle.
questions.note: For any circle it is a little over three times the diameter, and that ratio is pi.

questions.clue: This is a proposed explanation, put forward so that it can be tested by experiment.
questions.note: The plural is hypotheses. A theory in science is far stronger: an explanation that has already survived a great deal of testing.

questions.clue: This is the smallest particle of a substance that still has all the properties of that substance.
questions.note: Molecules are made of atoms. A water molecule is two hydrogen atoms joined to one oxygen atom.

questions.clue: This is the height of something measured above sea level.
questions.note: Altitude is usual for aircraft and elevation for ground features, but both answer the clue.

questions.clue: This is a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up itself.
questions.note: It is also used of a person or event that causes change, as in the catalyst for the reform.

questions.clue: This is the speed of an object measured in a particular direction.
questions.note: Speed alone has no direction, so it is not accepted here. A change in velocity over time is acceleration.
